clue.text: Eleven ways artist lifted

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting the letters means they are read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: lanes are routes or ways
RA is a Royal Academician, the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: Eleven routes on which a painter rose up.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal is a London football club, and a football side is an eleven.
explanation.definitionFit: A football team fields eleven players, so a club side such as this London one is an example of an eleven.

clue.text: By the sound of it, important little bird

indicators.note: asks us to go by what the words sound like when spoken, not how they are spelt

blocks.note: key means important and wee means little

explanation.surface: A tiny bird that seems to matter a great deal.
explanation.definitionFit: The kiwi is a flightless New Zealand species of bird.

clue.text: Prefer small group to secure a victory

indicators.note: securing something means holding it fast inside, so one part goes round the other

blocks.note: a foursome is a small group
A as written, and V is the abbreviation for victory

explanation.surface: Someone would rather a little team won the match.
explanation.definitionFit: To favour something is to like it better than alternatives, a straight synonym of prefer.

clue.text: Completely blooming accurate

blocks.note: flowers in bloom are said to be out
right means correct or accurate

explanation.surface: Totally, absolutely bang on, with blooming as a mild British intensifier.
explanation.definitionFit: Outright as an adverb means wholly or entirely, as in banned outright.

clue.text: Old music lover in band, her age mysterious

indicators.note: something mysterious is obscure and puzzling, so these letters are scrambled out of recognition

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An ageing fan plays in a group with a woman who keeps quiet about how old she is.
explanation.definitionFit: A headbanger is a heavy metal fan who shakes their head to the beat, here one past their youth.

clue.text: One of thirteen in England, I am on duty

indicators.note: says the solution sits inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: the last letter of England, the words I am on, and the first letter of duty

explanation.surface: A member of a thirteen-strong side announces they are working.
explanation.walkthrough: The thirteen suggests a rugby league team, but it is the thirteen cards of one suit in a pack.
explanation.definitionFit: Each suit in a standard pack of cards holds thirteen cards, so a diamond is one of thirteen.

clue.text: Test round part is going round

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the first part encloses the second

blocks.note: an oral is a spoken examination
a bit is a part

explanation.surface: Part of an exam is going round in circles.
explanation.definitionFit: Orbital describes something circling a planet or a city, so it means going round.

clue.text: Comfortable thing, executive admits, work on newspaper

indicators.note: admitting something lets it inside, so one part holds the other

blocks.note: a suit is slang for a business executive
a bed is a comfortable thing to lie on

explanation.surface: A boss admits something cosy is the job of a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: To subedit is to check and correct copy before it is printed, the job of a subeditor at a newspaper.

clue.text: Crazy meeting sane? Loco!

indicators.note: crazy suggests something wild and disordered, so these letters get jumbled

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone finds it mad to call a gathering sane, exclaiming that it is crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: Loco looks like slang for mad, echoing Crazy, but it is short for locomotive.
explanation.definitionFit: Loco is the short form of locomotive, and an old railway locomotive is driven by steam.

clue.text: Flier the police distributed close to Manchester

indicators.note: distributed things are spread about, so these letters are shuffled out of order
the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is used

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging
the final letter of Manchester

explanation.surface: Officers hand out leaflets near Manchester.
explanation.walkthrough: Flier looks like a leaflet, matching distributed, but it is something that flies.
explanation.definitionFit: A helicopter is an aircraft, so it is a flier in the sense of a thing that flies.

clue.text: Party saving minute deposit

indicators.note: saving something keeps it safe within, so one part holds the other

blocks.note: the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland
M is the abbreviation for minute

explanation.surface: A political party putting money aside as a down payment.
explanation.definitionFit: To dump something is to put it down or drop it, which is to deposit it.

clue.text: Bugs Bunny's opening song impressing cutie, occasionally

indicators.note: an opening is the start, so only the first letter of the name is used
occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is taken
impressing here means pressing into, so one part is pushed inside another

blocks.note: the first letter of Bunny
an aria is an operatic song
the first, third and fifth letters of cutie

explanation.surface: Bugs Bunny opens with a tune that wins over a sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: Bugs Bunny looks like the cartoon rabbit, but Bugs alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bugs is an informal word for germs or microbes, and bacteria are such microbes.

clue.text: Match decider ultimately in cup — might it be?

definitions.text: Match decider ultimately in cup — might it be?

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the word is used
in tells us one piece is placed inside another

blocks.note: a tie is a match, as in a cup tie
a beaker is a drinking cup
the final letter of decider

explanation.surface: Wondering what will finally settle a knockout game.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: in British football a cup match is a cup tie, and a drawn one needs settling.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiebreaker is an extra game, shoot-out or question used to settle a contest left level, such as a drawn cup match.

clue.text: Coarse ground initially wet

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter is taken

blocks.note: the first letter of ground
rainy weather is wet

explanation.surface: Rough soil, damp at first.
explanation.definitionFit: Grainy describes a rough, gritty texture, a synonym of coarse.

clue.text: Mobilisation of secret agent in prominent position

indicators.note: mobilising means setting in motion, so these letters are moved about

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A spy is deployed into a key spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Centre stage is the middle of a theatre stage, and figuratively the most prominent place to be.

clue.text: Magnificent job of truck, perhaps, carrying the Queen

indicators.note: carrying means bearing something within, so one part holds the other

blocks.note: a breakdown truck does towing
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A splendid feat by a lorry transporting the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Towering literally means very tall, and figuratively outstanding or magnificent, as in a towering performance.

clue.text: Nutty fruit

blocks.note: first meaning: crazy, informally
second meaning: the long yellow fruits

explanation.walkthrough: Nutty fruit sounds like something that tastes of nuts, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Going bananas is slang for going mad, and bananas are also the familiar tropical fruit.

clue.text: Perfect place for the swine, in fairness

blocks.note: to hone is to sharpen or refine to perfection
a sty is where pigs are kept

explanation.surface: An ideal pigsty, judged even-handedly.
explanation.definitionFit: Honesty means truthfulness and fair dealing, close in sense to fairness.

clue.text: In the distance, rank litter

blocks.note: far away means in the distance
a rank is a row or line

explanation.surface: Far off, a line of rubbish smelling rank.
explanation.walkthrough: Rank and litter suggest a smelly mess, but litter is the definition in its farmyard sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A farrow is a litter of piglets, and to farrow is for a sow to give birth.

clue.text: King George holding on, no ruler

indicators.note: holding means keeping something inside, so one part goes around the rest

blocks.note: GR is Georgius Rex, King George
on top of something is over it
taken as written

explanation.surface: A king clinging on to power, yet not really a ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: A governor is a person who governs a state or colony, and so a ruler.

clue.text: Book space

blocks.note: first meaning: one book in a set
second meaning: the amount of room something takes up

explanation.definitionFit: A volume is a single bound book, and also the measure of three-dimensional space something occupies.

clue.text: A cover turned over, revealing apple

indicators.note: turning something over flips it end to end, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
to lag pipes is to cover them with insulation

explanation.surface: Lifting a lid shows a piece of fruit underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Gala is a popular variety of sweet eating apple.

clue.text: Main villain in opera and songs from Germany on the radio?

indicators.note: the radio is heard and not seen, so we go by how the words sound

blocks.note: Wagner's Ring cycle of operas
lieder are German art songs

explanation.surface: The chief baddie in a broadcast opera with German songs.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringleader is the person heading a group of wrongdoers, the main villain among them.

clue.text: Flip that is a drink

indicators.note: flipping turns something round, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: that is gives it's, then a as written

explanation.surface: A flip is a cocktail, so someone names one as a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Flip is a real mixed drink, so it looks like part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine from Piedmont, so a drink.

clue.text: Hot stuff, a couple of letters to the auditor?

indicators.note: an auditor here is a listener, so we go by what is heard

blocks.note: the spoken names of two letters of the alphabet, K and N

explanation.surface: Racy material, perhaps a pair of letters sent to an accountant.
explanation.walkthrough: Auditor suggests an accountant checking books, but here it is simply a listener.
explanation.definitionFit: Cayenne is a fiery red pepper powder, so it is hot stuff in the culinary sense.

clue.text: Parrot I breed, it's caged

indicators.note: something caged is shut inside, so one part sits within another

blocks.note: taken as written
animals mate to breed
it, with the 's read as is joining the clue

explanation.surface: A bird keeper says they breed parrots and keep them in a cage.
explanation.walkthrough: Parrot looks like the bird, fitting caged and breed, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot is to repeat or copy mindlessly, which is to imitate.
